record.paper_title: Selected results and open problems in a semiclassical theory of dense matter
record.original_question: The SK theory currently yields, for a celestial object, only a physically allowed interval for the angular speed of rotation rather than a single predicted value. What additional theoretical structure, constraints, or calculational procedure would allow the theory to determine a unique angular speed of rotation for a given celestial object, instead of only an admissible interval?

evidence.quote: Another "‘open"’ astronomical application of the SK theory is the calculation of the angular speed of rotation of a celestial object. Instead of proposing an algorithm for this calculation and giving a unique number at the end,this theory gives a physically allowed interval in which the speed of rotation can be. It was applied to the Earth and several other planets. The results are very promising,but it would be useful to reduce this allowed interval to a unique number.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Within the semiclassical (SK) theory of dense matter, a self-gravitating celestial body in steady rotation is modelled as a fluid configuration whose mass density, pressure, and gravitational potential satisfy the SK equations of state together with the equilibrium (Euler/Poisson) equations in a frame rotating uniformly with angular speed ω. For a body of given total mass and chemical composition, requiring the existence of a regular, bounded, axisymmetric equilibrium with a free boundary determines not a unique value of ω, but a nonempty interval [ω_min, ω_max] of admissible angular speeds (as confirmed numerically when applied to Earth and several planets, where the observed rotation rate falls inside the predicted interval).

Problem. Formulate additional theoretical structure—extra physical principles, variational or stability criteria, boundary or matching conditions, or a constructive calculational procedure—within the SK framework that singles out exactly one element ω* ∈ [ω_min, ω_max] as the predicted angular speed of rotation of the body, and prove that the resulting prescription:
(i) yields a unique ω* for every celestial body to which the SK theory applies;
(ii) reduces the admissible interval to this single value in a manner consistent with all SK equilibrium equations; and
(iii) reproduces, in the cases where comparison is possible (such as Earth and the planets previously treated), the empirically observed rotation rates.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicitly open issue in the semiclassical (SK) theory of dense matter. A web search did not surface any subsequent work claiming to single out a unique angular speed of rotation from the SK-admissible interval; the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Selected results and open problems in a semiclassical theory of dense matter (arXiv abstract)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems of the SK theory, including reducing the predicted interval of angular rotation speeds to a unique value.
status_evidence.claim: The uniqueness of the predicted rotation rate is listed as an open problem with no resolution cited in follow-up literature found via search.
